subject: Separation of core work Packages vs dependencies imported from installed packages

messages.author: 31a23ff88538287b
messages.subject: Separation of core work Packages vs dependencies imported from installed packages
parts:
Something that I've noticed when using packages with Packrat is that when you load packages into your library, it also installs all the dependencies, which is fine, but makes it hard to differentiate
the core packages for a task, vs the imported dependencies. A good example is devtools, which imports a good amount of packages to use. Have you thought about making the Packrat Library displayed only the packages that you installed,
and maybe creating a sub folder for the dependencies so that while they are still there it does not clutter the packages pane in RStudio? 

These are just my thoughts, but I'd love to get others opinions on how, or what this would even look like.

Respectfully,

Peter Gensler

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: Separation of core work Packages vs dependencies imported from installed packages
parts:
Hi Peter,

One possibility would be to include a new column in the Packages pane, that denotes where / why a particular package is included in a project, but it would be difficult to get the UI exactly right without confusing users, I think.

Installing into a subfolder is also not that simple, since we want the default R workflows (using install.packages, install_github) to work as-is, and those install packages into the 'active' library path with the default behavior, which most users are accustomed to. We could potentially do something like add a new library path and separate packages according to 'used in this project' vs. 'a dependency of a package', but this would add a lot of overall complexity.

A starting point might just be a packrat function that returns the set of packages used / active in a project directly, and the dependencies of each of those packages.

Best,
Kevin

parts:
So is Packrat supposed to show just the packages that you installed in the Packrat Library in RStudio, plus that packages respective dependencies in the pane as well? Sometimes when Ive installed packages into my packrat library, my Packrat Library does not always refresh to show them, and sometimes it puts them all together. 

Let me think about this, as I think this feature can definitely be improved, as it is important for someone to see a package's dependencies from a debugging standpoint, but too many packages and all their dependencies really clog up their workspace. I may try to draw up something with Lucidchart, and share it with you if that is ok.
